text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: latency regression detected for /v1/generate p95=3200ms (baseline 700ms) — alert rule: api.latency.p95 > 1200ms
oncall-jason: acked, taking the incident. oncall status -> triage.
maria-sre: I'm grabbing traces and perf counters from the impacted hosts. tagging eu-west-1 pools.
tanya-eng: quick question, did we roll any kernel updates last night?
sam-runtime: yes, batch pushed kernel 6.6.4 -> 6.7.0 to pool-gpu-eu around 02:15 UTC.
oncall-jason: timeline note: paging started ~02:42 UTC, spike ramped until 03:10 UTC.
jordan-pm: customer impact: some Hosted API customers reported elevated p95 and a few client retries. CC billing for potential credits.
maria-sre: sharing trace snippets now — attaching spans (short).
maria-sre: ```
SpanTrace: request_id=abc123
- span[0] dispatch: 12ms
- span[1] model-infer: p50=180ms p95=3100ms
- span[2] kv-cache-miss: 8ms
- span[3] kernel-sched: wait=2.1s (tail)
```
tanya-eng: that's a huge tail on kernel-sched. can we get perf counters and run: `perf top`/`perf record`?
sam-runtime: pulling perf stat summary from one host: `perf stat -e context-switches,cpu-migrations,page-faults,cycles,instructions,cache-misses`
sam-runtime: ```
perf stat summary (host gpu-eu-12):
- context-switches: 1.2M (↑ 4x)
- page-faults: 18k (↑ 6x)
- cycles: 3.2e10
- cache-misses: 4.1e7 (↑ 3x)
```
maria-sre: also seeing increased softirq and higher runqueue lengths (runnable avg 5.6 vs baseline 0.8).
oncall-jason: mitigation: scaling up dedicated GPU workers in eu-west-1 by +30% and enabling fallback to smaller model variant for non-critical routes. executing now.
ops-bot: Scale operation started for pool-gpu-eu (requested +30%). ETA ~3m.
jordan-pm: please log exact customers/keys impacted so support can outreach.
maria-sre: collecting sample request ids and customer keys: 8 total customers, concentrated on eu-west-1. logs attached.
tanya-eng: hypothesis1: kernel scheduler regression in 6.7.0 causing longer context switch latency under high batching. hypothesis2: workload shift increased prefix-cache misses leading to blocking IO.
sam-runtime: to test kernel hypothesis, I'm spinning one host back to kernel 6.6.4 to compare. will rerun perf and trace after that.
oncall-jason: handoff: @maria-sre -> continue traces & perf, @sam-runtime -> kernel A/B test, @tanya-eng -> synth load to reproduce. I'll coordinate customer updates.
maria-sre: updated timeline in thread: 02:15 kernel rollout, 02:42 p95 climb begins, 03:04 alert threshold breached, 03:12 scale/up fallback run, 03:26 partial recovery on scaled hosts.
sam-runtime: A/B test result from host-27 (downgraded to 6.6.4): p95 on instrumented traces dropped to ~720ms. On 6.7.0 hosts p95 remained ~3k.
tanya-eng: that strongly points to kernel regression. collecting kernel trace (ftrace) to capture context-switch latencies.
jordan-pm: customer comms: sent initial status to ~8 affected customers, promise follow-up with RCA within 24h.
oncall-jason: post-incident actions: freeze kernel rollouts to all inference pools, expand canary checks, add perf baseline comparisons to deploy pipeline.
maria-sre: exporting full trace set and perf counters to shared incident bucket: gs://redwood-incidents/4109876543/traces.tar.gz
ops-bot: Incident status -> mitigated (partial) — monitoring.
oncall-jason: closing loop: keep this thread for RCA assembly. please append any additional logs/hypotheses. :thumbsup:
